name: maclaurin-chapel

building.title: Maclaurin Chapel, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 107's outline from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; used only to choose the crop box, to pick the building's own points (frame.near_outline) and to draw on the heightmap figure; the frame comes from the LiDAR.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the foot of the steps up to the glazed entrance between the chapel and the hall, on the street side (dsLbToS1nQd0 wide view); the LiDAR ground on the path there is 43.49-43.53 m, so ground is 43.5 and the model's y is 0 there; place.py puts it on the map

lidar.licence: Auckland Part 1 LiDAR (2024), OpenTopography NZ24_Auckland, doi:10.5069/G9HH6H8T: sourced from LINZ and licensed by Regional Software Holdings Limited for re-use under CC BY 4.0

aerial.licence: Auckland Central 0.06 m Urban Aerial Photos (2023): sourced from LINZ and licensed by Auckland Council for re-use under CC BY 4.0

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) within near_outline m of building 107's outline (2.5: the hall's flat roof reaches 1.5-1.7 m beyond the outline, which follows its walls, over a walk along each long side): centre = mean x/y of points higher than tower_above m and within tower_radius m (in plan) of the highest of them: the top of the chapel's low pyramid roof and the slender spire on it (a tree's crown over the south-west corner of the hall, 9 to 19 m up, is classed as building, so without tower_radius it pulls the centre 13.6 m away); axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls: the hall is nearly square and the chapel is many-sided, so their principal axis, 11.0 deg, is 8.8 deg off the hall's walls), the one of the two square to each other nearest the principal axis, pointing north-ish as street_side is west; toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: west-north-west, to Princes Street.

streetview.pano_ids_note: the five Google panoramas that show the building (2024-07, on Princes Street 32-41 m from the chapel, in front of its street side; 2026-10-22). Of the 50 Google panoramas within 120 m, the 19 within 70 m were looked at in a low-resolution probe (zoom 3, 118 tiles, 110 of them bought): these five show the chapel and the hall, a sixth on the same row (2YsL7HxV6pA9, 40 m) only the tree in front of it, and the 13 others (Princes Street further off, Waterloo Quadrant 2026-04) trees, at most the spire's tip. User-contributed panoramas are not used.

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins): the five panoramas were taken on a July (winter) morning with the sun low in the north-east, behind the building as seen from Princes Street (it flares in JYSz's wide view, at about bearing 40 deg): so the street faces are in open shade; exposure 0.78 brings the plain white face of dsLb's upper view to the photograph's luma (154; 180 at 1.0)

ground_note: the LiDAR ground on the path at the foot of the entrance steps (43.49-43.53 m); the street side runs from 43.5 there to 43.8 at either end of the building, and the back falls to 42.9; frame thresholds are above this ground (0.1 m higher than with the first, provisional 43.6, so the frame is the same)
